bullets.title: AMD: Citi upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $575 on GPU momentum and META deal
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Hold to Buy and raised its price target to $575 from $460, citing AMD as a legitimate GPU second source with a ~4-year META deal; first gigawatt ramps expected 2H26/2027 at ~$15B per gigawatt revenue. Citi's revised CY26/27/28 EPS estimates are 12-13% above Street consensus, and its CPU 2030 TAM model was raised to $137B from $132B.

bullets.title: ADBE: CFO departure + organic ARR cut trigger broad PT reductions; NTM P/E collapses to 8.5x
bullets.body: Adobe beat Q2 EPS/revenue and raised FY26 guidance, but cut organic ARR guidance by ~$500M via the Semrush acquisition and announced CFO departure (CEO search already ongoing), triggering ~11% average PT cuts across the Street. Sell-side now 37% Buy; Citi lowered PT to $228 (9.1x FY27 EV/FCF), Mizuho to $245, Wells Fargo to $250, RBC to $285. AI-first ARR is growing ~3x y/y but represents <2% of total ARR; NTM P/E at 8.5x vs 5-yr avg 26x.

bullets.title: ANET PT raised to $190, CSCO to $130 at Morgan Stanley on inference-driven front-end networking refresh
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised Arista's PT to $190 (from $180) and Cisco's PT to $130 (from $120), arguing AI inference workloads are driving a front-end network refresh cycle starting with cloud then enterprise. AI agents produce 450% the traffic of humans; Dell'Oro estimates AI front-end networking spend grows from ~$1.8B (2025) to ~$6.3B (2030) at 29% CAGR. ANET targets $3.5B and CSCO $4B in AI revenue for FY26.

bullets.title: COHR: Record bookings, CY27 booked out, NVDA partnership multi-billion through decade
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-weight on COHR at $330 PT but flags high demand visibility: record bookings in Q2/Q3, CY27 effectively booked out with visibility extending into 2028. NVIDIA partnership provides a multi-billion-dollar revenue stream through end of decade backed by a $2B equity investment; plan to double internal InP output by calendar year-end then more than double again by CY27. CPO concerns seen as overblown by both MS and Citi; optical content grows regardless of CPO/NPO architecture timing.

bullets.title: ORCL: -8.5% on high capex / limited EPS upside; EPS beat but analyst issues Sell
bullets.body: Oracle reported Q2 EPS of $2.03 vs. consensus $1.96, but shares fell ~8.5% on concerns about peak capex with limited EPS upside and uninspiring FY27 guidance reiteration. One analyst maintained a Sell citing overvaluation despite the beat. Oracle also faces scrutiny from a Google-identified ShinyHunters breach of PeopleSoft software (May 27–Jun 9).

bullets.title: NVDA: Sharon AI signs 6-yr compute deal; Vera CPU pivot for China after GPU restrictions
bullets.body: Sharon AI announced a six-year strategic compute collaboration with NVIDIA, signaling continued long-duration demand commitments. Separately, NVIDIA is pivoting to Vera CPUs for the China market after GPU export restrictions limited revenue there, with multiple Chinese customers expressing interest. Token price deflation near-term weighs on AI infrastructure sentiment but COHR's NVIDIA partnership and AI factory orders for 2027-2030 support multi-year capex cycle.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi bullish post-CFO meeting; Q2 commercial snapback expected, $225 PT (71.7% upside)
bullets.body: Citi remains bullish on Palantir after a CFO meeting, expecting a Q2 commercial booking snapback after Q1 was weighed down by USG resource diversion to Middle East conflict. AIP traction in North America and internationally continues; new wins include neoclouds and Kirkland & Ellis (legal). Palantir targets Rule-of-100+ metrics (80%+ growth + 60% margins). Citi PT is $225.

bullets.title: MU: JPM buyside survey ahead of Jun 24 F3Q26 earnings; consensus F4Q26 revenue $41.4B
bullets.body: JPM is surveying buyside expectations for Micron's F3Q26 earnings (Jun 24). Bloomberg consensus has F3Q26 revenue at $34.7B, gross margin at 81.4%, and EPS at $19.8 vs. JPM's guided $33.5B/$81%/$19.15. F4Q26 consensus: revenue $41.4B, gross margin 82.9%, EPS $24.1. DRAM ASP rose mid-60s% QoQ and NAND ASP high-70s% QoQ in F2Q26.

bullets.title: KLAC: 326% unusual options volume spike; INTC +9% on GOOGL EMIB packaging deal
bullets.body: KLAC saw options volume 326% above its 30-day average (9,197 vs. 2,825 contracts) with a 0.65 put/call ratio. Morgan Stanley flagged INTC +9% on a Google EMIB packaging deal and KLAC +13% on a Samsung partnership as key semi-equipment moves; semiconductor ETF SOXL alone generated ~$12B in rebalancing demand equal to ~45% of prior-day AUM.

bullets.title: GOOGL/META/AMZN: Citi top online ad picks into Cannes; U.S. online ad spend +16% Y/Y in 2026E
bullets.body: Citi names GOOGL, AMZN, META, RDDT, and APP as top picks into Cannes '26, forecasting U.S. online ad spend accelerating to +16% Y/Y (from +13% in 2025). Google launched five new AI Search ad formats and its Universal Cart for agentic commerce; AI Mode queries run ~3x longer than traditional, creating richer intent signals. Meta faces escalating litigation risk after a California court upheld a $6M jury verdict on adolescent social media addiction with thousands of cases pending and punitive exposure.

bullets.title: AAPL: iOS 27 confirms foldable iPhone; Apple's AI uses own AFM models, not Google infrastructure
bullets.body: KeyBanc notes iOS 27 beta confirms foldable iPhone references with ~10M first-year shipments and higher margins expected. Apple's collaboration with Google on Siri AI uses Apple's own distilled Foundational Models (AFM Core on-device, AFM Cloud on servers)—not Google's apps, infrastructure, or search—clarifying the competitive dynamic.

bullets.title: DKNG: Wells Fargo raises 2028+ estimates on prediction market TAM expansion; Indiana May GGR +15% Y/Y sports
bullets.body: Wells Fargo raises 2028+ estimates for DraftKings on expanding prediction markets TAM as more leagues recognize PMs as official operators; DKNG expected to increase marketing during World Cup and release vertically-integrated products by NFL season. Indiana May sports betting GGR was +15% Y/Y though DKNG's own share slipped to 36% from 37%, while FanDuel grew to 15.1% hold (+290bps Y/Y).

bullets.title: ALAB/CRWV/NBIS added to Nasdaq-100; CHTR removed
bullets.body: Astera Labs (ALAB), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Nebius (NBIS) are being added to the Nasdaq-100 index, while Charter Communications (CHTR) is being removed. ALAB is +290.7% YTD near a 52-week high; CRWV and NBIS are also rallying on the addition news.

bullets.title: ADBE/INTU/CRM/TTD at 52-week lows; software bifurcation widening vs. AI infra winners
bullets.body: 52-week low screen flags ADBE (-7.8% today, -51.1% YTD), INTU (-2.5%, -64.7% YTD), CRM (-1.3%, -38.2% YTD), and TTD (-1.7%, -74.3% YTD) among 27 stocks at new lows. Software/IGV down 0.72% on the day while AI Winners index gained 5.75% and SOX +7.9%, underscoring the widening bifurcation between AI infrastructure and traditional software.

bullets.title: ENPH: Jefferies flags $15/share upside from AI data center SST pivot, but adoption post-2027
bullets.body: Jefferies highlights Enphase's pivot toward solid-state transformers (SSTs) for 800V DC architectures in AI data centers as a potential $15/share upside catalyst, though commercial adoption is likely post-2027 and the market is highly competitive with ABB, Siemens, and Schneider as incumbents. ENPH's residential solar business remains under pressure.

bullets.title: SHOP: Jefferies sees SHOP as agentic commerce leader with SMB LLM discovery and enterprise traction
bullets.body: Jefferies frames Shopify as an early AI commerce leader benefiting from SMB discovery via LLMs, growing enterprise traction, and internal AI-driven efficiency with monetization optionality. The note is constructive on SHOP's positioning ahead of the next wave of agentic commerce adoption.

bullets.title: TSM: Supply chain risk from China tungsten/WF6 embargo; zero Japan semiconductor gas output
bullets.body: Japan's semiconductor gas production fell to zero after China cut off tungsten supply, with TSMC, SK Hynix, and Samsung supply chains at risk. A separate report notes China export controls on WF6 have shut down a Japan supply chain affecting chip production. These represent escalating supply-chain weaponization risks for the semiconductor sector.

bullets.title: TSLA: GLJ maintains Sell with $24.86 PT; Q2 delivery rebound seen as inventory-driven, not organic
bullets.body: GLJ Research's Gordon Johnson kept Tesla on Sell Alert with a $24.86 price target, arguing that the expected Q2 delivery improvement reflects inventory clearing and seasonal demand rather than renewed underlying strength. No change in the bearish thesis.

bullets.title: AVGO: Back-end supply issues affecting v9 Google TPU roadmap
bullets.body: UBS flagged that Broadcom is facing back-end supply constraints that are affecting the v9 generation roadmap for Google TPUs. Anthropic/OpenAI data center ASIC capacity (where Broadcom is a key player) could reach ~13GW by C2028, implying ~$130-190B in revenues, but supply execution is an emerging gating factor.

bullets.title: Mag 7 premarket all higher; token deflation and AI supply wave (SpaceX, GOOGL, OpenAI IPOs) create near-term headwinds
bullets.body: All Mag 7 stocks are trading higher premarket (GOOGL +1.3%, META/AMZN +1%, TSLA +0.7%, MSFT/NVDA +0.6%, AAPL +0.4%), and five of seven Mag 7 names are on Bearish TREND per Hedgeye. Near-term headwinds include a supply wave from SpaceX/$75B IPO and potential OpenAI/Anthropic IPOs worth hundreds of billions, plus token price deflation hitting infrastructure-heavy names. Tech adjusted for AMZN/GOOGL/META now exceeds 51% of S&P 500.
